newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BROKERS GRAPPLE WITH 48-HOUR SETTLEMENT, MORE OUT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BROKERS GRAPPLE WITH 48-HOUR SETTLEMENT, MORE OUT.

text.p: Fiat justitia, pereat mundus. Athens stock exchange member brokers are finding it practically very difficult to meet a tight 48-hour settlement deadline when it comes to foreign client orders and face the risk of repeated non-compliance and expulsion from trade.

On Wednesday, Sigma Securities, the Athens bourse's leading broker in terms of market share so far this year, Hermes Brokerage and Epsilon Securities were not allowed to trade after failing to deliver shares on time.
And on Tuesday, five other brokers including N. Devletoglou Securities and Nuntius, both very active with foreign funds, faced similar problems and were barred from trading for one day.

"We are being punished for not delivering shares by 14:30 local, when the clearing house closes, even though we had the shares at 15:00 hours after an agonising rush with our client's global and local custodians," said Nuntius managing director Alexander Moraitakis.
The problem is especially acute when it comes to orders from U.S.-based institutional clients.

Aside from the time zone difference, the back office procedure involves a fund's global custodian who has to instruct their local custodian in Greece to confirm that a trade execution on the fund's behalf by the local broker is correct before releasing money or shares.
This often fails to make full circle within the tight 48-hour deadline and allow the Athens broker to meet the unreasonable T+2 settlement rule.

"Foreign institutionals are not allowed by law to release shares in advance, they must strictly observe the delivery versus payment rule," Moraitakis points out, noting that the problem could become frequent and further exacerbate brokers.

Sigma Securities failed to deliver on time securities worth 36 million drachmas and was not allowed to trade on Wednesday. But the firm does about 9-10 percent of the bourse's trading volume on average, which translates to amounts over a billion drachmas daily, its officers said.
"We were not allowed to trade on Tuesday because we failed to deliver shares to the clearing house within 48 hours after the sale," Alexander Devletoglou told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We had sales from our foreign clients ang got the shares from their custodians at 15:00 local but the bourse had closed at 14:30, so we delivered the next morning and were penalised," he said.
Hermes brokerage managing director Anastasios Siafakas also slammed authorities for being unfair and selective when it came to penalising brokers for non-compliance with settlement regulations.

"What is being done is unfair and selective. The bourse picked three brokers today and barred them from trade when based on the same criteria it should have barred 31 brokers. And do note that two of these happen to be state bank subsidiary brokerages," Siafakas told Reuters.
"It is an unfair practice which denigrates Athens stock exchange members," he said.
The third firm that was barred from trading on Wednesday was Epsilon Securities. It was not allowed in the session for similar reasons.
"The clearing house demands delivery of shares in 48 hours but it does not practice what it preaches. It fails to hand us securities bought in 48 hours," said analyst Dimitris Tsouvalas at Epsilon.

"So when I do trades on behalf of foreign clients I cannot get paid on time by their custodian since I do not have the shares from the clearing house on time. It is an unacceptable situation. Brokers must thus bear the cost of the clearing house's flaws," he said. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
